mechanism_principle.content: The positive misfit between the FCC matrix and precipitate causes the formation of a parallel raft microstructure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C

mechanism_principle.content: Rafting of γ′ precipitates is attributed to the positive lattice misfit between γ and γ′ phases.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Therefore, the rafting of γ′ in HESA has shown to coarsen along the direction of the applied stress, which can be related to the positive lattice misfit (δ) between γ and γ′

mechanism_principle.content: The lower creep strain rate is explained by the energetically favorable partial dislocations and increased spacing between them due to lower SFE, making bowing around particles more difficult.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: For materials possessing lower SFE, partial dislocations are more energetically favorable, and the spacing between partial dislocations can be increased. As a result, the dislocations bowing around γ′ particles would become more difficult, which effectively decreases the creep strain rate.

mechanism_principle.content: The lower creep rate is attributed to the sluggish diffusion of the high entropy gamma matrix and the un-rafted gamma prime microstructure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Therefore, the possible sluggish diffusion of the higher entropy γ matrix and the un-rafted γ′ microstructure can contribute to lower creep rate.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that the HESA is strengthened by low stacking-fault energy, high anti-phase boundary energy, and a thermally stable microstructure.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Analysis on experimental results indicate that HESA could be strengthened by the low stacking-fault energy of the matrix, high anti-phase boundary energy of the strengthening precipitate, and thermally stable microstructure.

hypothesis_statement.content: Future alloy designs involving minor additions of gamma partitioning elements like Mo and Re are expected to lead to negative lattice misfit and solid-solution strengthening.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: For the future alloy designs, the minor addition of γ partitioning elements like Mo and Re would lead to the desirable negative lattice misfit for N-type rafting of γ′ and also provide solid-solution strengthening to the γ matrix [54]

evidence_result.content: The creep behavior of HESA is dominated by tertiary creep.

evidence_result.content: Average size of spherical γ′ precipitates measured by image analysis is 290 nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The γ′ precipitates appears to be spherical with an average size of 290 nm and 69 vol% measured by image analysis.

evidence_result.content: Lattice misfit of HESA at 982 °C calculated from XRD data is 0.08%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Therefore, by the calculation of δ = 2 ( a γ ′ − a γ ) / ( a γ ′ + a γ ) , where δ is the lattice misfit between γ and γ′, a γ and a γ ′ is the lattice constant of γ and γ′ phase, respectively, the lattice misfit of HESA at 982 °C is 0.08%.

evidence_result.content: The linear fitting slope of composition plot (0.62) matches the experimentally measured γ′ volume fraction, validating the chemical composition measurements.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The linear fitting slope in Fig. 3(b) is 0.62, which is close to the γ′ volume fractions measured experimentally, so the validity of the measured γ and γ′ compositions has been demonstrated.

evidence_result.content: Calculated reduction of stacking fault energy (SFE) due to alloying is 1.5 times greater in HESA compared to CMSX-2.
evidence_result.evidence_span: By applying the γ compositions in Table 1 into the above model, the value of Δ Γ γ ( x ) are −1.0 and −0.67 for HESA and CMSX-2, respectively, indicating that the reduction of SFE in the Ni-based FCC matrix due to alloying in HESA can be 1.5 times greater than that of CMSX-2.

evidence_result.content: APB energy of γ′ phase in HESA (0.22 J/m²) is higher than in CMSX-2 (0.19 J/m²).
evidence_result.evidence_span: According to JMatPro calculations, the APB energies of γ′ phase in HESA and CMSX-2 are 0.22 and 0.19 J/m 2 , respectively.

evidence_result.content: HESA possesses higher tensile yield strengths than CoCrFeMnNi and the highest among reported high entropy alloys.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The precipitation strengthening has allowed HESA to possess higher tensile yield strengths than those of CoCrFeMnNi throughout the temperatures. Furthermore, the tensile yield strengths of HESA are the highest among reported high entropy alloys.

evidence_result.content: Creep rupture life of HESA at 982 °C is about 114 hours.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The creep rupture life of HESA at 982 °C is about 114 h

evidence_result.content: Creep activation energy for HESA estimated from the slope of ln ε ˙ vs. T −1 is 290 kJ/mol.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From the linear slope of ln ε ˙ vs. T −1 curve, the creep activation energy of HESA can be estimated to be 290 kJ/mol

evidence_result.content: Dislocations pile up within the γ matrix without shearing the γ′ phase at 982 °C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 8(b) shows the TEM analysis of crept HESA at 982 °C; dislocations have mainly piled-up within the γ matrix with no shearing the γ′ phase.

evidence_result.content: At 750 °C and 850 °C, γ′ morphology remained spherical with no rafting observed after 800 h creep.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Moreover, the morphology of γ′ has remained spherical, indicating that no rafting of γ′ has occurred in both conditions.

contradiction.content: The observed creep behavior of HESA (P-raft dominating tertiary creep) is contrary to the expectation that P-raft is beneficial for thermal cyclic creep resistance.
